mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and investor confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 5.0% signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and decline in the unemployment rate (indicating aggressive monetary tightening during a strong labor market) increases borrowing costs and reduces liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by rising FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of monetary tightening cycles (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects expanding manufacturing output and economic growth, supporting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger Federal Reserve rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad economic slowdown, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and INDPRO does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (characterized by strong nonfarm payrolls growth), the S&P 500 experiences positive returns as companies benefit from robust consumer demand and pricing power over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of late-cycle expansions (t-test p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).
